title: Grab and move blocks some shortcuts
author: davidgilbertson

status.label: Focused fix hypothesis is ready for design approval
status.detail: Grab and Move configured for Alt consumes or reorders Alt-first keyboard sequences used by AutoHotkey and shell Alt-drag, even after two earlier hotfixes.

next_action.label: Approve the focused fix direction
next_action.reason: The fast judgment identifies a repository change, while implementation-grade design remains deferred.

judgment.rationale: The issue has multiple concrete public reproductions, survived the intended hotfix, and includes a maintainer statement that related input infrastructure must change.
evidence: Reporter retested after PRs 47261 and 47326 and said the original issue remains.
PR 47261 releases retained Alt state on other interactions.
AutoHotkey and shell Alt-drag examples demonstrate that non-mouse consumers receive the wrong modifier sequence.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the focused design direction, then run the full issue-to-design workflow before implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No current upstream or fork implementation fully covers the reproduced interaction.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Alt state for unrelated keyboard combinations while Grab and Move waits for a mouse gesture
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Grab and Move hook temporarily owns Alt activation state and replays/releases it for selected transitions, but unrelated keyboard combinations can observe a missing or reordered Alt down/hold sequence.
plan: Trace low-level keyboard events for Alt-first multi-modifier input with Grab and Move enabled.
Separate pending drag activation from unrelated keyboard combinations and replay the absorbed Alt event before forwarding the non-mouse key sequence.
Preserve the existing suppression of window-menu activation only after an actual drag/resize gesture.
Add regression coverage for AutoHotkey-style Alt combos and shell Alt-drag alongside normal Grab and Move activation.
verification: Run the issue's Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Q AutoHotkey sequence with Alt pressed first and confirm it fires once.
Alt-drag a file to create a shortcut and confirm the shell receives the modifier.
Verify Alt+mouse drag still moves/resizes and does not activate the window menu afterward.

confidence.rationale: The public reproduction and prior hook fixes identify the interaction boundary, but exact event ordering still requires a maintainer trace.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move configured for Alt consumes or reorders Alt-first keyboard sequences used by AutoHotkey and shell Alt-drag, even after two earlier hotfixes.
known_information: The original Alt-first Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Q sequence fails only while Grab and Move is enabled.
The reporter confirmed the hotfix did not resolve the issue.
A maintainer said the solution is expected to resemble the earlier fix but needs infrastructure changes.
Other commenters reproduce failures for Alt-to-text and Alt-drag shortcut creation.
inferences: Grab and Move's activation hook likely absorbs the Alt transition and does not restore a continuously held modifier before forwarding unrelated keyboard input.
The exact failure varies by consumer because event ordering, not the downstream shortcut definition, is likely corrupted.
issue_context.analysis: The discussion and merged PR descriptions identify the key-event replay boundary well enough for a focused design proposal, while a trace must still confirm ordering for multi-modifier sequences.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all public comments.
Inspected the linked Grab and Move fixes and related issue relationships.
Used the public reproductions to separate confirmed symptoms from the hook-order root-cause hypothesis.

actions.label: Trace Alt event ordering with Grab and Move

reproduce.version_requirements: Latest stable PowerToys and a current AutoHotkey v2 build
prerequisites: Enable Grab and Move with Alt as activation modifier.
Enable the option that prevents Alt from activating the window menu.
Create a harmless AutoHotkey Alt-first shortcut such as Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Q showing a message.
steps: Run the shortcut with Alt pressed before the other modifiers and record low-level key down/up ordering.
Repeat with Grab and Move disabled.
Repeat Alt-dragging a file to create a shell shortcut.
Repeat an actual Alt+mouse drag to verify Grab and Move activation.
reproduce.expected_result: Unrelated Alt keyboard combinations and shell Alt-drag receive a normal held-Alt sequence, while actual Grab and Move gestures retain menu-suppression behavior.
